text.p: SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - The German Foreign Ministry has confirmed that Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel will pay a two day visit to Slovakia, starting May 1. Kinkel is expected to meet Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, President Michal Kovac and his Slovak counterpart Pavol Hamzik.

NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, has not named the Asian investor interested in purchasing the Slovak stake in Czech commercial bank Komercni Banka. The paper says the investor could be Japanese investment bank Nomura.

- The government is expected to announce a series of economic measures to react to the Czech economic recovery plan, approved last week, which is expected to hurt Slovak exports to the Czech Republic.

- The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said the government move to suspend preparations for a referendum on direct presidential election was wrong and that according to Slovak law challenging the referendum's legitimacy before the Constitutional Court cannot delay the plebiscite.
- London-based SG Warburg has sold its 10.87 percent share in major Slovak paint producer Chemolak a.s. but gave no reason for the move.

- Slovakia's major opposition parties have issued a joint statement calling for a 'yes' vote on Slovakia's NATO membership in the forthcoming referendum. The opposition said entry to NATO would return Slovakia to the European community and would bring security and economic stability.

- Shares of Slovakia's second largest commercial bank, IRB a.s., will be excluded from a Central European Stock Index (CESI), effective April 30, due to low liquidity. The CESI index reflects development of the most liquid stocks on bourses in Bratislava, Prague, Warsaw, Budapest and Ljubljana.

- Some 169,857 privatisation bonds were sold in direct trades since the beginning of this year. Only 4,419 privatisation bonds were matched in anonymous trades, while the market registers some 240,387 orders to sell the bond.

SME - The oppositin Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) has repeatedly accused the finance ministry of preparing an amendment to a law on the National Bank of Slovakia which would transfer banking supervision from the central bank to the ministry.
- Supreme Control Office (NKU) Chairman Stefan Balejnik said ministries and other state authorities did not respect NKU's rulings.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The overall amount of liabilities of the National Property Fund totalled 111.3 billion crowns at the end of last year. The fund approved 209 direct sales of state property in 1996, with revenue from the sell-offs totalling 16.4 billion crowns.

- The Union of Small Businesses said it would stick to its threat to stop all contributions to the state budget and funds, such as insurence and pension funds, if the government ignores its demand to start a dialogue on problems of small entrepreneurs. The contribution from around 100,000 union members can total up to 300 million crowns.
